extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals; PRSA members; communications practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of PRSA's ethics resources, the PRSA Code of Ethics' core values, BEPS advisory role, and a list of Ethical Standards Advisories (ESAs) that apply the Code to specific practice issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA Code of Ethics — core values
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRSA Code of Ethics sets out principles and guidelines that uphold the core values of the ethical practice of public relations, including advocacy, honesty, loyalty, professional development and objectivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Code exists to inspire ethical behavior and to provide examples of malpractice, inappropriate and unethical behavior; BEPS upholds and amends the Code as needed and offers educational opportunities to explore ethics year-round.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of unethical/improper/malpractice conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Unethical, improper, malpractice: A threat to the ethical practice of public relations; Behaviors inappropriate or inconsistent with the Code; Behaviors disruptive or that undermine ethical practices; Practices and behaviors destructive to the reputation of practitioners, our profession or Society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Code is intended to clearly identify malpractice and other improper behaviors and to warn and teach members how to avoid them.

rubrics_metrics.name: BEPS role and remit
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizing and acknowledging ethical issues as they arise is among the reasons the PRSA Board of Ethics and Professional Standards (BEPS) was created; BEPS provides resources (case studies, ESAs, quizzes, blogs) and is a sounding board for chapter ethics officers and members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS upholds and amends the PRSA Code, provides educational opportunities (e.g., Ethics Month, conference sessions), and responds to member inquiries (allow three weeks for response).

rubrics_metrics.name: ESAs are binding extensions of the Code
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical Standards Advisories (ESAs) are considered direct extensions of the PRSA Code, and have the same force and effect as any provision within the PRSA Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ESAs are designed to keep the PRSA Code timely through a formal process and provide practitioners guidance to deal with new situations and circumstances as they arise in the daily practice of public relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use BEPS decision-making resources
rubrics_metrics.description: BEPS Handbook includes tools such as Eight Ethics Questions to Ask Yourself Before Acting; Six Statements That Should Warn You of a Potential Ethical Violation; Six Indications That Your Company Has an Ethical Culture; Eight Ethics Quotes; Six Practical Recommendations for Building Employer Branding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These resources and discussion guides (case studies, matrix of ethical dilemmas, discussion guides) are intended to help practitioners recognize dilemmas and choose ethical actions before acting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure (ESA, 2018)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure (2018)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As an ESA, this advisory applies the PRSA Code to disclosure-related issues. ESAs serve as current-practice guidance with the same force as Code provisions and are used to address new circumstances in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and Social Media (ESA, 2015)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethics and Social Media (2015)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses how PR ethics apply in social media contexts; ESAs provide specific guidance to apply Code principles to evolving platforms and practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and Transparency in Native Advertising and Sponsored Content (ESA, Sept. 2014)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure and Transparency in Native Advertising and Sponsored Content (September 2014)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides guidance on disclosure and transparency obligations when producing native advertising or sponsored content, as an extension of the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deceptive Online Practices and Misrepresentation of Organizations and Individuals (ESA, Rev. June 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deceptive Online Practices and Misrepresentation of Organizations and Individuals (Rev. June 2012)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises practitioners on avoiding deceptive online conduct and misrepresentation; ESAs clarify how Code principles apply to digital deception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegal Recordings (ESA, March 2011)
rubrics_metrics.description: Illegal Recordings (March 2011)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on the ethical implications and prohibitions related to making or using illegal recordings in PR practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Use of Interns (ESA, February 2011)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical Use of Interns (February 2011)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises on fair, ethical treatment and appropriate use of interns consistent with the Code's values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism (ESA, Sept. 2010)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism (September 2010)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies expectations and prohibitions around plagiarism and proper attribution as applied under the PRSA Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Looking the Other Way (ESA, Aug. 2010)
rubrics_metrics.description: Looking the Other Way (August 2010)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses the ethics of ignoring or failing to act upon observed unethical conduct; ESAs provide examples and guidance for responding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expropriation of the Intellectual Property of Others (ESA, Feb. 2010)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expropriation of the Intellectual Property of Others (February 2010)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on respecting intellectual property rights and avoiding improper appropriation of others' IP in PR work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Video News Releases as a Public Relations Tool (ESA, Oct. 2009)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of Video News Releases as a Public Relations Tool (October 2009)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises on ethical considerations and disclosures when distributing video news releases to media or the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questionable Environmental Claims and Endorsements (Greenwashing) (ESA, Oct. 2009)
rubrics_metrics.description: Questionable Environmental Claims and Endorsements (Greenwashing) (October 2009)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides guidance to avoid misleading environmental claims and endorsements; applies Code standards to environmental communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay for Play (ESA, Oct. 2009)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay for Play (October 2009)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses disclosure and ethical issues when payments or incentives are used to obtain media coverage or endorsements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engaging in the Use of Deceptive Practices While Representing Front Groups (ESA, Rev. Oct. 2008)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in the Use of Deceptive Practices While Representing Front Groups (Rev. October 2008)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns against representing front groups or using deceptive practices and explains how the Code applies to such conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overstating Charges, Fees and/or Compensation (ESA, rev. Aug. 2007)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overstating Charges, Fees and/or Compensation (rev. August 2007)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides practitioners on accurate representation of fees, charges and compensation to avoid misleading clients or the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure by Expert Commentators and Professional Spokespersons of Payments or Financial Interests (ESA, April 2005)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure by Expert Commentators and Professional Spokespersons of Payments or Financial Interests (April 2005)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses transparency requirements for experts/spokespersons regarding payments or financial interests that might influence commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telling the Truth, Especially in War Time (ESA, Jan. 2005)
rubrics_metrics.description: Telling the Truth, Especially in War Time (January 2005)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reaffirms the obligation to tell the truth and examines ethical tensions that arise in wartime communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting Unethical Behavior or Unprofessional Performance (ESA, Nov. 2004)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting Unethical Behavior or Unprofessional Performance (Nov. 2004)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides guidance on when and how to report observed unethical or unprofessional conduct consistent with the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Employment Status of Client-Based PR Agency Staff (ESA, May 2004)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of Employment Status of Client-Based PR Agency Staff (May 2004)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises on disclosure obligations when agency staff are presented in ways that might obscure their employment relationship with a client.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA approach: education and inspiration over formal sanctioning
rubrics_metrics.description: PRSA moved away from identifying violators and sanctioning in 2000; the revised code focuses on education, inspiration and motivating ethical behavior rather than enforcement because voluntary organizations lack legal authority to enforce sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because PRSA is a voluntary organization with limited enforcement authority (unable to subpoena evidence or impose legally backed sanctions), the Code emphasizes examples, descriptions of malpractice, and education rather than punitive enforcement; PRSA reserves the right to expel a member only if found guilty of misconduct in a court of law.
